dialogues.speaker: Ei
dialogues.text: Many challenges still lie ahead for Inazuma, but I am prepared for them.

response.speaker: Ei
response.text: Abolishing the Sakoku Decree has a myriad of implications. It would be folly to say that it will be all positive, and there will be no negative repercussions.

response.speaker: Ei
response.text: For example, I can foresee the outside world posing a threat to Inazuma's businesses. These are the issues that I must work to solve.

response.speaker: Yae Miko
response.text: Ei, you're thinking about this all so conscientiously. I've only got as far as wondering whether I'll be able to sell entrance tickets to the Grand Narukami Shrine in the future.

response.speaker: Ei
response.text: Honestly, Miko...

choices.text: About the gaze of the gods...

response.speaker: Ei
response.text: Makoto's gaze was always fixed on the people of Inazuma. I always assumed it was because... that was her duty.

response.speaker: Ei
response.text: But now I see that hers was a gaze full of delight and hope. It was not just a duty, but a joy, too. She loved humanity very dearly.

response.speaker: Yae Miko
response.text: If people of the past deserved the gods' attention, then so do the people of the future.

response.speaker: Ei
response.text: Indeed. No longer will I ignore their passions and dreams.

response.speaker: Ei
response.text: To put it bluntly, it was constant torture with no end in sight.

response.speaker: Ei
response.text: Faced with an endless battle, I had to remain focused at all times. Had my concentration lapsed for but a moment, the Shogun's blade would have taken my life.

response.speaker: Ei
response.text: Safe to say, were it not for my previous experiences in combat, my skills would not have been up to the challenge. I would most certainly have been defeated.

response.speaker: Ei
response.text: And through it all, you also had your part to play.

choices.text: About the damage to the Sacred Sakura...

response.speaker: Ei
response.text: Don't worry, I haven't forgotten. I will be sure to remind the Tenryou and Yashiro Commissions of their duties in this regard.

response.speaker: Ei
response.text: It's not only the monsters that I am worried about. I'm concerned about what else might escape from the Sacred Sakura.

response.speaker: Yae Miko
response.text: That's a tough one, alright... There's plenty more besides memories held in the Ley Lines.

response.speaker: Ei
response.text: Since you clearly understand, perhaps you could think about making an effort, too.

choices.text: Yae Miko said she was placing her god—

response.speaker: Yae Miko
response.text: Ahem! Yae Miko said nothing of the sort, and the Traveler has some nerve making up spurious claims about her while she is still present.

response.speaker: Yae Miko
response.text: Some words are not to be passed on.

response.speaker: Yae Miko
response.text: Trust me, you don't want to know the cost of betraying me. Just think of the things I said to you as our little secret. Understood?

response.speaker: Ei
response.text: What are you talking about?

response.speaker: Yae Miko
response.text: Nothing. I suddenly want some fried tofu.
